newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank cuts overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank cuts overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank announced on Tuesday a cut in its overnight borrowing and lending rates.
The Central Bank said it cut the overnight borrowing rate to 10.4375 percent from 10.5 and its overnight lending rate to 12.9375 percent from 13.0 percent.
Bank dealers said the cut in overnight rates was widely expected.

"In fact, the Central Bank had conditioned the market for this impending slash when it cut its reverse repo rates and yields on its 90-day special series treasury bills on Thursday," said one trader at a foreign bank.

The trader said the adjustment of the Central Bank's rates "seemed imminent" after the Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate dipped to an average of 10.564 percent at Monday's regular weekly Treasury-bill auction from 10.625 percent last week.
On tuesday, the Central Bank also lowered yields on its three-day and one month reverse repos, which were both pegged at 10.5 percent from the previous 10.5625 percent.
The rate on the two-month reverse repo also dipped to 10.5625 percent from 10.625 percent.
The Central Bank made a new offer for 57-day special series T-bills at 10.4 percent.
However it withdrew its 86-day and 38-day special series T-bills which were previously pegged at 10.6 percent and 10.5 percent, respectively.
